body.statement: For every finite \(G\), the capsule assignment can be sampled in polynomial time, and finite enumeration of all capped reservoir draws and remaining fair coins computes every \(\pi_u\), every entry of \(\Gamma_G\), and every conditional weight defining \(\widehat\tau_G\) exactly; hence the design--estimator pair is total and evaluable without observing internal focal metadata.
body.justification: The information-theoretic theorem must correspond to a finite experiment and an estimator measurable in the published data regime.
body.gap: The prior seed construction required an explicit Rao--Blackwell enumeration audit; the balanced capsule changes both the latent support and the conditional weights.
body.consumer: Exact small-instance evaluation provides a reproducible audit and a benchmark for scalable approximations.
body.proof_tex:
Fix a finite revealed graph \(G\).  One trial samples a uniform \(k\)-subset, computes its radius-two forbidden union by at most \(k\) breadth-first searches of depth two, and checks whether the remaining set has at least \(k\) vertices.  After at most \(n^3\) trials, drawing \(C\), the arm-swap coin, and at most \(n\) remaining fair coins also takes polynomially many elementary operations.  Thus an exact sample from \(\mathsf D_G^{\mathrm{cap}}\) is produced in time polynomial in \(n\) (and hence in \(n\) and \(d\)).

For exact finite evaluation, let \(\Omega_G\) be the finite latent sample space consisting of the ordered list of at most \(n^3\) proposed reservoirs, the accepted reservoir and \(C\) when acceptance occurs, the arm-swap coin, and the remaining assignment coins.  Every atom \(\eta\in\Omega_G\) has an explicitly known rational probability under \(\text{def:reservoir-capsule}\), and the maps
\[
\eta\longmapsto Z^{\mathrm{cap}}(\eta),\qquad
\eta\longmapsto X_u(\eta)
\]
are deterministic.  Consequently the finite sums
\[
\pi_u=\sum_{\eta\in\Omega_G}\Pr(\eta\mid G)X_u(\eta)
\]
and
\[
\Pr(X_u=X_v=1\mid G)
=\sum_{\eta\in\Omega_G}\Pr(\eta\mid G)X_u(\eta)X_v(\eta)
\]
compute every inclusion probability and, through \(\text{def:normalized-kernel}\), every entry of \(\Gamma_G\) exactly.  This enumeration is finite, although it is not asserted to be polynomial-time.

Finally fix an observed atom \(o=(G,z,y(z))\), and let
\[
\Omega_G(o)=\{\eta\in\Omega_G:(Z^{\mathrm{cap}}(\eta),y(Z^{\mathrm{cap}}(\eta)))=(z,y(z))\}.
\]
Proposition \(\text{prop:capsule-realization}\) ensures that every endpoint appearing in \(\widetilde\tau_G(\eta)\) for \(\eta\in\Omega_G(o)\) is among the observed coordinates in \(o\).  Hence
\[
\widehat\tau_G(o)
=\frac{\sum_{\eta\in\Omega_G(o)}\Pr(\eta\mid G)\widetilde\tau_G(\eta)}
       {\sum_{\eta\in\Omega_G(o)}\Pr(\eta\mid G)} \tag{8}
\]
is an explicit finite sum whenever the denominator is positive; it is positive for every realized observation.  Equation (8) computes the Rao--Blackwell conditional weights using only \(G,z,y(z)\), not the unobserved focal metadata.  This proves totality and exact finite evaluability.
